AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #11
====

GRADE: Grade 5
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Conserving Wild Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Conserving Wild Animals.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Conserving Wild Animals.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Conserving Wild Animals.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Conserving Wild Animals.

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cooking Food Frying Frying? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cooking Food Frying Frying.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Cooking Food Frying Frying.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cooking Food Frying Frying.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking Food Frying Frying.

3. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Nitrogen gas only

4. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Decomposers only
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Producers

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Food Nutrients 10 2.5 Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Good Grooming Pra? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Food Nutrients 10 2.5 Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Good Grooming Pra.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Food Nutrients 10 2.5 Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Good Grooming Pra.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Food Nutrients 10 2.5 Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Good Grooming Pra.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Food Nutrients 10 2.5 Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Good Grooming Pra.

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Uses of Domestic Animals 8 2.3 Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nu? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Uses of Domestic Animals 8 2.3 Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nu.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Uses of Domestic Animals 8 2.3 Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nu.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Uses of Domestic Animals 8 2.3 Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nu.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Uses of Domestic Animals 8 2.3 Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nu.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Soil Conservation? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Soil Conservation.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Soil Conservation.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Soil Conservation.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Soil Conservation.

8. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 0 °C

9. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Milk souring
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Ice melting to water

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nutrients 10 2.5 Cooking Food 9 3? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nutrients 10 2.5 Cooking Food 9 3.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nutrients 10 2.5 Cooking Food 9 3.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nutrients 10 2.5 Cooking Food 9 3.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nutrients 10 2.5 Cooking Food 9 3.

11. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

12. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water always increases oxygen

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Preservation of Cereals and Pulses? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Preservation of Cereals and Pulses.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Preservation of Cereals and Pulses.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Preservation of Cereals and Pulses.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Preservation of Cereals and Pulses.

14. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water Conservation? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water Conservation.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water Conservation.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Water Conservation.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water Conservation.

16. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. joule (J)
   C. watt (W)
   D. newton (N)

17. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Uses of Domestic Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Uses of Domestic Animals.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Uses of Domestic Animals.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Uses of Domestic Animals.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Uses of Domestic Animals.

18. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

19. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Growing Vegetables? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Growing Vegetables.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Growing Vegetables.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Growing Vegetables.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Growing Vegetables.

20. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Good Grooming Practices 7 3.2 Home Hygiene 9 3.3 Laundering Cotton Item 10 4.0 P? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Good Grooming Practices 7 3.2 Home Hygiene 9 3.3 Laundering Cotton Item 10 4.0 P.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Good Grooming Practices 7 3.2 Home Hygiene 9 3.3 Laundering Cotton Item 10 4.0 P.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Good Grooming Practices 7 3.2 Home Hygiene 9 3.3 Laundering Cotton Item 10 4.0 P.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Good Grooming Practices 7 3.2 Home Hygiene 9 3.3 Laundering Cotton Item 10 4.0 P.

21. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Food Nutrients? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Food Nutrients.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Food Nutrients.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Food Nutrients.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Food Nutrients.

22. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
23. In three clear sentences, explain Conserving Wild Animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Growing Vegetables and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Uses of Domestic Animals 8 2.3 Preservation of Cereals and Pulses 10 2.4 Food Nu and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
